svg.title: Manufacturing routes – which part gets which operation
svg.text: Routing matrix (example) – filled = operation in the route, number = sequence
CNC plasma 6 mm plates; no furnace (9.3 m) – flame straightening; pads milled on long bed
plasma 10–15 mm, UT butt welds, SR 580–620 °C, boring mill one set-up
housing welded 30–40 mm, preheat 75–100 °C; bores Ø140 H7; wheel turned + hardened
laser 6–12 mm, jig-welded; roller axle bores + rail faces machined
small frame; pulley + roller bores machined
laser-cut / profiles, few welds; slide faces + racks machined, straight ≤ 0.5
tube + end discs welded, SR, turned + grooves; shaft 42CrMo4 turned + ground
Quality frame (example): ISO 3834-3 shop, EN 1090-2 EXC2 as practice, welders ISO 9606-1, WPS per ISO 15614-1, ISO 5817 level C (B at the mast foot + wheel blocks)
NDT: VT 100 % (ISO 17637) · MT 20 % main fillets + 100 % mast foot (ISO 17638) · UT 100 % full-pen butt welds (ISO 17640) – check EN 1090-2 Table 24 minimum
Surface: Sa 2½ (ISO 8501-1), roughness medium G (ISO 8503), C3 (ISO 12944-2), EP primer 80 µm + PUR top 80 µm = 160 µm NDFT, machined faces masked + oiled
Hold points: material certificates 3.1 (EN 10204) · fit-up · dimensional report after welding · after stress relief · after machining · NDT report · DFT report
